rule.title: View function reads slot mutated mid-execution by a sibling writer that issues an external call

intent.attack_thesis: A writer function issues an external call before finalizing a storage slot update (state-after-external-call pattern). A downstream protocol that reads the same slot via a view function mid-execution observes stale or intermediate state, which it uses to make economic decisions — enabling price manipulation or collateral mispricing across protocols.

reporting.title_template: Read-only reentrancy: view function exposes mid-mutation state to downstream protocols
reporting.summary: Matches a writer function that mutates a slot via state-after-external-call paired with a view function reading the same slot, exposing stale state to downstream oracle consumers.
reporting.user_summary: This contract updates important state (like price or balance) after making an external call, and exposes that state through a view function. A downstream protocol reading this view function during the update window will see an inconsistent, mid-transaction value — enabling price manipulation and mispriced collateral decisions.
reporting.technical_summary: The detector joins a writer function matching the state-after-external-call pattern on a price/reserve/totalSupply slot with a view function reading the same slot. The combination creates a read-only reentrancy surface exploitable by protocols that rely on the view function for price or collateral calculations.
reporting.exploit_narrative: An attacker calls the writer function of contract A (e.g., a liquidity pool). During the external ETH callback, the attacker calls contract B (a lending protocol) which reads A's view function to price collateral. A's state is mid-mutation — the view returns stale/manipulated data. Contract B misprices collateral, enabling undercollateralized borrowing.
exploit_preconditions: writer function issues external call before finalizing price/balance slot
view function is called by downstream protocol during execution
downstream protocol makes value decisions based on the stale view
remediation_hints: add a nonReentrant modifier to the writer function to prevent callback re-entry
update all price/reserve/totalSupply slots before making external calls (CEI pattern)
downstream protocols should use time-weighted values rather than spot view reads

preconditions: writer function with external call before state finalization
downstream protocol reads view function of this contract for pricing

steps.action: call writer function; in external call callback, call downstream protocol that reads view function
steps.expected_state: downstream protocol observes stale/mid-mutation price from view function

steps.action: exploit mispriced collateral or liquidity in downstream protocol
steps.expected_state: attacker extracts value from downstream protocol using stale price

witness_goal.success_condition: attacker profits from price manipulation of downstream protocol via read-only reentrancy
